A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work. Their main text, equations, five experimental figures, two tables, and appendices are readable and support comparison; v2 adds Appendix E.

before.justification: Section 3.2 and Appendix D report original neural density-ratio estimation experiments on synthetic Gaussian distributions, including L1, L2, and L3 errors across 100 trials.

after.justification: Section 3.2 and Appendix D retain these original experiments and their reported error curves, including results for multiple dimensions and mixture modalities.

M1.justification: The conceptual mu-representation loss, practical f-divergence optimization, and early-stopping framework are retained. Appendix E's suggestions for generative models do not introduce an implemented method component.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate synthetic Gaussian density-ratio estimation with the same KL-divergence and dimensionality sweeps and one to four numerator modes. The newly discussed GAN and normalizing-flow applications are not evaluated.

E2.justification: The experiments retain the same KL-divergence and alpha-divergence loss comparisons. The anonymous alpha-divergence reference becomes Kitazawa (2024), identifying the same method. Methods newly discussed in Appendix E are not added to the experiments.

E3.justification: The reported synthetic-data calibration changes from mu = sqrt(KL(P||Q)) in v1 Appendix D to mu = sqrt(2 KL(P||Q)) in v2 D.1. This corrects a stated generation setting; the PDFs do not establish that experiments were rerun. Splits, sample sizes, metrics, and training budgets are retained.

E4.justification: The analyses of sensitivity to KL divergence, dimensionality, sample size, and mixture modality are retained in Figures 1–5. No additional ablation, robustness experiment, or empirical case study appears.

E5.justification: Both versions report 100 trials and summarize errors using medians and interquartile ranges. There is no change to repeated-run information or statistical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Figures 1–5 retain identical plotted results. However, Section 3.2 and the appendix results text correct the reported contrast from rapid growth for p > 0 and mild growth at p = 0 to p > 1 and p = 1. This corrects the description of existing findings rather than reporting a performance gain.

T1.justification: Appendix E.2 adds Assumption E.1 and formal derivations concerning local smoothness and strong convexity. v2 also changes Equation (6)'s exponent from (1-p)/p to (p-1)/p, repairs Jensen steps in Equation (16) and Appendix C, revises stochastic orders in the C.18 proof, and corrects Table 2's Pearson conjugate term. The rewritten C.5 inequality introduces a missing distance factor.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution statement, and conclusion retain the same central claims: common Lp error bounds across f-divergence losses, dependence on dimensionality and KL divergence, and numerical corroboration.

C2.justification: New Appendix E explains how the assumptions relate to pointwise versus expected-loss convexity and proposes a Fisher-information interpretation. It also recommends RMSE/MSE over MAE for benchmarking and suggests fitting base distributions for f-GANs and normalizing flows. These substantially extend the interpretation and proposed applicability of unchanged experiments.

D1.justification: The corrected mean-offset formula in Appendix D changes the instructions for reproducing synthetic data. Architecture, optimizer, hyperparameters, NVIDIA T4 hardware, and the statement that experimental code accompanies the supplementary material are otherwise retained.

R1.justification: Appendix E substantially expands positioning through explicit comparisons with kernel and nearest-neighbor DRE bounds, pseudo-self-concordance, and potential generative-model applications. Added references include Kanamori et al., Kpotufe, Lin et al., and Bach. The introduction also expands its treatment of Nguyen et al.'s existing bounds.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, main-results exposition, conclusion, and experimental descriptions undergo extensive sentence and paragraph rewriting. v2 also integrates Appendix E through cross-references, repairs subsection and equation references, and standardizes terminology and notation.

P2.justification: Figure 1 moves alongside Figure 2, appendix figures are redistributed around implementation text, and captions are rewritten. The experimental graphics themselves and the basic structures of both tables are retained; no figure or table is added.

improvement.justification: Corrected Jensen algebra, data-calibration instructions, and expanded research context provide clear local benefits. However, the rewritten C.5 condition requires 1/L <= |T*(y)-T*(x)| for every x,y, which fails at x=y and conflicts with C.20's distance-scaled condition. This new defect concerns the central lower-bound assumptions, making the net quality effect of the theoretical revisions uncertain.
